items.title: OpenAI cuts GPT-5.6 Sol API pricing by 20%+
items.summary: OpenAI dropped GPT-5.6 Sol API pricing for the next three months: input falls from $5 to $4 per million tokens, output from $30 to $20. The cut also applies to ChatGPT Work and Codex credit plans; Pro/Plus/Business subscriptions are unchanged. It's OpenAI's second price cut in under a month, following late-July reductions on Terra and Luna, as it responds to competition from Anthropic and Chinese labs.
items.whyItMatters: GPT-5.6 Sol is the tier OpenAI routes complex prompts to from its realtime voice stack (per GPT-Live's design), so a 33% output-price cut directly lowers the cost of any fallback-to-text-reasoning path Romain leans on.

items.title: Nari Labs pushes open Qwen3-TTS to sub-50ms time-to-first-audio
items.summary: Nari Labs open-sourced an optimized serving stack for Qwen3-TTS (1.7B CustomVoice) that hits sub-50ms p95 time-to-first-audio at 10 requests/sec on a single H100 — beating vLLM-Omni, SGLang-Omni, VoxServe and others. Techniques include trimming leading silence, a unified scheduler across the Talker/Code Predictor/Codec stages, urgency-aware prioritization, and CUDA-graph kernels for the codec's fixed-step structure. Cost works out to roughly $2 per 1M characters, versus $100 (ElevenLabs V3) or $49 (Cartesia Sonic 3.5).
items.whyItMatters: This is a direct playbook for shaving latency out of a self-hosted TTS leg — the scheduler/urgency-aware-prioritization trick in particular is applicable to any pipeline juggling ASR, LLM, and TTS stages the way Romain and Anna do, and the open-sourced code is a concrete alternative if ElevenLabs/Cartesia costs become a bottleneck.

items.title: DeepSeek ships V4-Flash-Vision-Exp, a cheap multimodal model near Opus 4.8 on agent benchmarks
items.summary: DeepSeek released V4-Flash-Vision-Exp on its API, an experimental multimodal model that matches V4-Flash on text/reasoning while making a large jump on multimodal agent benchmarks, landing close to Claude Opus 4.8 on some of them. It's a sparse MoE (13B active / 284B total params) with a 1M-token context, priced at $0.22/M input and $0.66/M output on OpenRouter, alongside a new free Files API for reusable image uploads.
items.whyItMatters: A cheap, capable vision model with a million-token context is a plausible building block for a French-tutor feature idea — e.g. photograph a French menu, sign, or worksheet and have the tutor discuss it — at a fraction of frontier-model image pricing.
